title: The Biggest Bomb Ever: A Cloud 7 Times Higher Than Everest
description:
Unreal but true: a new real event every day at 5:48 pm (Riyadh).

On October 30, 1961, the Soviet Union tested the Tsar Bomba over Novaya Zemlya in the Arctic. At 50 megatons it is the most powerful weapon ever detonated. It exploded about 4 km above the ground, and its mushroom cloud rose to about 64 km (40 miles), roughly seven times the height of Mount Everest. The blast wave travelled around the Earth three times.

It was a test over a remote Arctic test range; the sources below report no deaths.

Sources give the cloud height as about 64 km (Atomic Heritage Foundation), about 67 km (Wikipedia) and more than 60 km (Britannica). The counter in the video is not in real time.

Sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / National Museum of Nuclear Science & History, "Tsar Bomba"; Encyclopaedia Britannica, "Tsar Bomba"; Wikipedia, "Tsar Bomba". Scale marks (approximate): Mount Everest 8.85 km, passenger jets about 11 km, Concorde 18 km, SR-71 about 26 km, weather balloons about 35 km, highest skydive 41.4 km (Alan Eustace, 2014), top of the stratosphere about 50 km.
Animation drawn in code; narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs).

Did you guess it? Tell me your number in the comments.
